title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act aims to boost the creation and sharing of AI technologies as open‑source projects. By offering incentives and legal protections for open‑source AI research, the act encourages innovation, transparency, and collaboration across the industry.

title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a law that bans the development, deployment, or use of certain artificial intelligence systems defined as "covered AI." It aims to protect public safety and privacy by restricting these systems without stringent oversight.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress detailing how artificial intelligence systems are used to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will evaluate the scope, effectiveness, and legal compliance of these AI tools in the context of national security surveillance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building new large-scale data centers dedicated to AI, aiming to curb rapid expansion and its environmental impacts. By halting construction, the act provides time to develop comprehensive regulations, safety guidelines, and sustainable infrastructure standards for AI operations.

title: A bill to require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill requires every company or organization that develops or uses artificial intelligence to build a way for a human to immediately shut the system down. This ensures that if an AI behaves unexpectedly or poses a risk, a person can stop it before it causes harm.

title: To require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disclose each instance in which the Secretary uses artificial intelligence to interact with a covered individual, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The policy requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to publicly disclose every time AI is used to interact with a covered individual. It also mandates disclosure for other uses of AI within the Department, ensuring transparency and accountability.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act seeks to halt the development and deployment of AI systems that could act outside of human control or cause harm, by setting strict safety and oversight requirements. It establishes licensing, monitoring, and enforcement mechanisms—including penalties and possible dismantling—to ensure any AI operating under this law meets rigorous risk‑mitigation standards.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act would prohibit the construction or operation of AI data centers on federally owned property, preventing the use of public land for these high‑energy‑intensive facilities. This measure aims to preserve federal land for other purposes and reduce the environmental and security impact of large AI infrastructure projects.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is designed to shield households from the rising electricity bills caused by the operation of large AI data centers. It proposes regulations that would limit the amount of power these facilities can draw or require them to offset their energy usage, ensuring that families do not face higher energy costs.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to protect consumers and workers by outlawing AI companies from charging excessively high prices and manipulating wages. The law would create oversight and penalties to ensure fair pricing and equitable labor practices in the AI industry.

title: To better coordinate Federal efforts to utilize advance technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve diagnoses, treatments, cures, and prevention strategies for pediatric cancer, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy aims to improve coordination among federal agencies so they can more effectively use advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to enhance diagnosis, treatment, cure, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It also seeks to broaden these efforts to other related healthcare goals by streamlining resource sharing and collaboration across the federal system.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a federal program to study how artificial intelligence is used in the judicial system and to identify any risks or biases. It also creates an independent oversight body that will monitor AI tools in courts, set guidelines for their use, and ensure transparency and accountability for decisions made with AI support.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy says that every American and local community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial‑intelligence data center has a right to full transparency about those activities. It also requires that those communities retain local autonomy, ensuring they can influence how the data center impacts them.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is a U.S. law aimed at protecting proprietary AI models from theft and unauthorized use. It establishes penalties, reporting requirements, and protective measures to encourage companies to secure their AI technologies.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act seeks to shield the electoral process from harmful AI‑generated misinformation. It establishes rules for identifying, limiting, and penalizing deceptive AI content that could sway voters or undermine confidence in election outcomes.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a federal law that seeks to regulate the design, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence across the United States. It sets out safety, transparency, and accountability requirements for companies, mandating risk assessments, disclosure of AI capabilities, and oversight mechanisms to protect public interests and promote ethical AI practices.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: Congress supports the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, affirming it as a strong policy to safeguard consumers and keep electricity affordable. The resolution also stresses that all U.S. communities, from households to farms, must maintain access to reliable, affordable power amid the growth of AI and data centers.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 proposes regulations to promote the adoption of liquid cooling technologies in AI data centers to improve energy efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. It outlines standards for design, safety, and compliance to ensure new AI infrastructure can operate more sustainably while maintaining performance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a federal law that requires AI developers and operators to evaluate and reduce the environmental footprint of their systems, from data center energy use to hardware lifecycle impacts. It sets standards for reporting, promotes green AI technologies, and imposes penalties for non‑compliance to protect ecosystems and public health.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is designed to set clear rules for how data can be used to train and run AI systems, with a focus on transparency and accountability. It introduces standards for data collection, usage, and protection to help safeguard privacy and promote responsible AI development.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies to evaluate how automated decision systems affect fairness, privacy, and safety. It sets up rules for transparency, auditing, and reporting so that algorithms can be monitored and corrected to reduce bias and protect users.
